title: SCHD’s Rules Sold Broadcom in March 2024. The Stock Is Up About 183% Since, and SCHD Holders Missed the Run
summary: SCHD's rulebook kicked out one of the market's hottest chip stocks before its biggest run, and the reason it happened reveals a hidden cost that no expense ratio will ever show you.

title: What Are Applied Materials Stock Investors Overlooking?
summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) sold a record $7 billion of chipmaking tools in fiscal Q3 2026. That was about 77% of its $9.1 billion in revenue for the quarter. When you own the stock, you mostly own those tool sales. A record that large is easy to read as the new normal. So what might Applied Materials investors be overlooking about those tool sales.

title: What Is The Case For Waiting On Qualcomm Stock?
summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) stock is up 46% over six months. It still trades about 26% below its high of the past year. At 21 times earnings, about the market's level, the price appears to assume Qualcomm keeps growing as Apple sales shrink. Qualcomm plans to fill that gap with car and data center chips, and is raising prices as memory costs climb. Both plans are under way. So is there a case for waiting before you buy Qualcomm.

title: These Nasdaq 100 Stocks Are Quietly Paying Real Dividends
summary: Most investors write off the Nasdaq-100 as a dividend wasteland, but a handful of its chip and networking giants have been quietly raising their payouts every single year while competitors chase hype cycles.

title: Is Applied Materials Still The Business You Bought?
summary: You may own Applied Materials (AMAT) as a chip equipment maker that aims to hand most of its spare cash back to shareholders. A $10,000 holding a year ago is now worth about $24,500. Your stake in this business is far bigger than it was. Is Applied Materials still the business you bought.

title: NVIDIA's Stock Gains 1.7% as It Unveils Historic Buyback
summary: NVDA gains 1.7% after unveiling a record $150 billion buyback expansion, lifting remaining repurchase capacity to $235 billion through fiscal 2028.

title: ON Semiconductor Stock Looks Expensive Until You Price Its Fuller Factories
summary: ON Semiconductor (ON) makes power and sensing chips for cars, industrial equipment and AI data centers. The stock trades at about 27.6 times trailing adjusted earnings, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back. That basis is meant to sit closer to the one analysts use in their forecasts than GAAP earnings would, though the two are not defined identically. At that multiple the stock looks expensive. But the trailing year was weak, and the weakness is fading.

title: 67-Year-Old Costs Himself $1,315 A Year In Taxes Using A Treasury Fund To Add $1,000 A Month In Income To His Social Security And Pension. If He’d Used SCHD Instead His Tax Bill Would Be Reduced By Over 60%
summary: A retired man collects Social Security and a pension, adds $1,000 a month from a popular Treasury fund, and ends up handing the IRS a bill he never needed to pay. The fund type is the culprit, and the fix is hiding in plain sight.
